- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price action shows resilience.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak values by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias in subsequent days.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag; add 1–2% downward adjustment to early forecast days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend, not just price history.
